shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures traded in a tight range on Tuesday, as traders weighed a rise in oil prices against steady but cautious downstream demand.($1 = 159.7800 yen)($1 = 6.7205 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures traded in a tight range on Tuesday, as traders weighed a rise in oil prices against steady but cautious downstream demand.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
little changed at 441.2 yen ($2.76) per kg as of 0209 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 75 yuan, or 0.4%, to 18,950 yuan ($2,819.73) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 455 yuan, or 3.1%, to 15,125 yuan per metric ton.
Oil prices gained on Tuesday as renewed fighting between the U.S. and Iran in the Middle East raised fears of supply disruptions from the world's key crude-producing region.
Natural rubber often follows oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.

Production is projected to rise 2.1% to 15.28 million tons and consumption 0.4% to 15.36 million tons, leaving the market in a slight deficit for the rest of the year, data from the Association of Natural Rubber Producing Countries (ANRPC) showed in its latest report.

The downstream tire industry's operating rate in top rubber producer China remains stable, though companies are sticking to essential purchases of natural rubber, analysts from broker Shanghai Zhongqi Futures said in a note.
End-user demand remains only moderate and purchasing sentiment cautious, which may cap further price gains, analysts from broker Gelin Dahua said in a note.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 236.8 U.S. cents per kg, up 0.1%.
